literal: Impermanent is the nature of wealth; if that is obtained, things that endure, immediately, should be done.
translation: Wealth is of an impermanent nature; if you obtain it, immediately perform those deeds that are of a lasting nature.
modern: செல்வம் நிலைவில்லாத தன்மையுடையது; அதனைப் பெற்றால், அப்பொழுதே நிலைத்து நிற்கும் அறச்செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the fleeting nature of material wealth and advises on its immediate, wise utilization. The word 'அற்கா' means impermanent or non-abiding, describing the true nature ('இயல்பிற்று') of wealth ('செல்வம்'). Since wealth can vanish at any moment, the author urges that if one happens to acquire it ('அதுபெற்றால்'), they must immediately ('ஆங்கே') use it to perform deeds that have a lasting value ('அற்குப செயல்'), such as acts of virtue and charity. By converting transient wealth into enduring good deeds, one achieves something of permanent value before the opportunity slips away.
